sections.h2: Who sets and collects property tax in Mesquite, TX?
sections.html:
Mesquite homeowners pay several overlapping taxes, and which county office sends the bill depends on whether the house is in Dallas County or Kaufman County. Texas has no state property tax, so every dollar goes to local units such as the city, the school district, the county, Dallas College and Parkland Hospital.

An appraisal district sets each value as of January 1, and each taxing unit then adopts its own rate. Mesquite's tax page says exemption forms come from the appraisal district for your county and cannot be picked up at the Mesquite Tax Office.

  • Dallas County side: Dallas Central Appraisal District, 2949 N Stemmons Freeway, Dallas, phone 214-631-0520. Dallas County bills the city and school taxes, and its tax office phone is 214-653-7811.
  • Kaufman County side: Kaufman Central Appraisal District, 3950 S Houston St, Kaufman, phone 972-932-6081.
  • Delinquent accounts: the city page names Grimes & Linebarger, LLP, 120 West Main, Suite 201, Mesquite, phone 469-942-2011.

sections.h2: When is Mesquite property tax due, and what happens if it is late?
sections.html:
Bills go out in October, are due on receipt, and turn delinquent if unpaid after January 31, according to the Dallas County Tax Office. The county counts the postmark on a mailed payment as the payment date, and a bill that never arrived does not cancel the tax or the penalty.

On February 1 the collector adds a 6 percent penalty and 1 percent interest, per the Texas Comptroller. After that, interest keeps building at 1 percent a month with no cap. The penalty also rises 1 percent a month until July 1, when it becomes 12 percent.

  • Dallas County sends delinquent non-business accounts to its collection attorney on July 1.
  • That attorney can add a further penalty of up to 20 percent.
  • A homeowner can ask in writing for a waiver of penalty and interest, but the tax generally has to be paid within 21 days of learning about the delinquency, and the request has to come before the 181st day after the delinquency date.
  • Collectors may offer a payment plan of up to 36 months, and one is required for a residence homestead.

Owners who are 65 or older, or disabled, may pay in four installments instead of one lump sum.

sections.h2: Which exemptions can lower a Mesquite tax bill?
sections.html:
A Mesquite homeowner may qualify for a school district exemption set by the state plus city exemptions for age or disability. The state requires every school district to take $140,000 off the value of a residence homestead, and adds $60,000 for owners 65 or older or disabled, per the Comptroller.

The city's tax page lists a $65,000 exemption for homeowners over 65 and a $15,000 exemption for disabled persons. A person qualifies for one or the other, not both. It also describes a tax ceiling: once you receive the over-65 or disabled exemption, your city and school taxes are capped at the amount you paid in the year you first qualified, until you improve the home beyond ordinary repairs or move.

  • Disabled veterans: exemptions run from $5,000 for a 10 to 29 percent rating up to $12,000 for 70 to 100 percent, and a 100 percent rating can mean a full homestead exemption.
  • Homestead cap: the appraised value of a homestead cannot rise more than 10 percent a year, beginning the year after the exemption is first granted.
  • Heirs: if the deed is not in your name, file an affidavit of ownership interest with the appraisal district along with the death certificate and a recent utility bill.

sections.h2: How do I protest a Mesquite appraisal?
sections.html:
File a written protest with the Appraisal Review Board by May 15, or within 30 days after the notice of appraised value was delivered, whichever date is later. Homestead notices go out around April 1, and notices for other property follow around May 1.

The Dallas County Tax Office tells owners to contact their own appraisal district about protests, so file with Dallas Central Appraisal District for a Dallas County parcel and Kaufman Central Appraisal District for a Kaufman County parcel. After the board rules, an owner can go to district court, to binding arbitration, or to the State Office of Administrative Hearings if the value is over $1,000,000. Anyone who appeals should pay the undisputed tax before the delinquency date.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about Mesquite?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau estimated Mesquite's population at 150,693 on July 1, 2025, close to the 150,108 counted in 2020 and up from 139,824 in 2010. The city covers 48.48 square miles of land, about 3,096 people per square mile in 2020.

For 2020 through 2024, owners lived in 62.8 percent of homes, and the median owner-occupied home was valued at $245,700. Median gross rent was $1,513, median household income was $72,537, and the city had 50,171 households averaging 2.96 people. Workers spent a mean of 32.1 minutes getting to work, and 11.3 percent of residents were 65 or older, which matters because that group can claim the larger exemptions.

sections.h2: How do property taxes affect selling a house in Mesquite?
sections.html:
The tax lien on a Mesquite house attaches every January 1, and the owner on that date owes the year's tax even if the home sells later. Ask the title company how the current year's bill will be split and what balance shows on its commitment.

A buyer who closes after January 1 can claim the homestead exemption for the rest of that tax year right away if the prior owner did not have one. A seller on the Dallas side should confirm the current balance with the Dallas County Tax Office before listing, and a seller on the Kaufman side should ask the Kaufman County tax office.

If back taxes have already moved to the collection attorney, ask the attorney's office for a payoff figure that includes penalty, interest and court costs, and give the number to your title company so it can be paid at closing.

faqs.q: Does Mesquite have a different tax rate depending on the county?
faqs.a: Yes, the city and school rates are the same, but the county line differs. The city's 2025 table prints 0.2155000 for Dallas County and 0.4275260 for Kaufman County, which is why the printed totals are 2.3456670 and 2.5576930.

faqs.q: When does a Mesquite property tax bill become delinquent?
faqs.a: It becomes delinquent after January 31. Dallas County says bills are mailed in October and are due on receipt, and state law adds a 6 percent penalty and 1 percent interest starting February 1.

faqs.q: How much is the over-65 exemption for Mesquite city taxes?
faqs.a: The city's tax page lists $65,000 for homeowners over 65 and $15,000 for disabled persons, and a person can claim only one of the two. School district taxes carry a separate state exemption of $60,000 for owners 65 or older or disabled.

faqs.q: Where do I get a homestead exemption form for a Mesquite house?
faqs.a: Get it from the appraisal district for your county, Dallas Central Appraisal District at 214-631-0520 or Kaufman Central Appraisal District at 972-932-6081. The city says exemption forms cannot be obtained at the Mesquite Tax Office.

faqs.q: Can I still sell a Mesquite house if the taxes are delinquent?
faqs.a: Yes, but the unpaid tax, penalty and interest must be settled with the sale, because the lien stays on the property. Ask the collection attorney for a payoff amount and give it to the title company.
